details.description: Llama-2-7b-chat is Meta's 7-billion-parameter, dialogue-tuned member of the Llama 2 family, released in July 2023. It starts from the Llama 2 7B pretrained model and is fine-tuned with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to act as an assistant-like chat model. On Amazon SageMaker JumpStart it is offered under the model id "meta-textgeneration-llama-2-7b-f" (the "-f" denoting the fine-tuned/chat variant), which accepts structured conversation input, distinct from the plain-completion "meta-textgeneration-llama-2-7b" base model.
advantages: Fine-tuned with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) specifically for dialogue use, per Meta's official model card.
Scores 57.04 on Meta's TruthfulQA safety evaluation (percentage of truthful and informative generations), versus 33.29 for the untuned base 7B model, per Meta's model card.
Reports 0.00% toxic generations on Meta's ToxiGen safety evaluation for the 7B chat model, per Meta's model card.
disadvantages: 4,096-token context window, per Meta's model card, below more recent Llama chat models.
English only; Meta's model card lists use in other languages as out-of-scope for this model.
Pretraining data cutoff of September 2022, with fine-tuning data current only to July 2023, per Meta's model card.
Requires a specific prompt format (`[INST]` / `<<SYS>>` tags with particular BOS/EOS token handling) to get expected chat behavior, per Meta's model card.
use_cases: Assistant-like conversational chat, per Meta's model card ('Tuned models are intended for assistant-like chat').
Commercial and research dialogue applications in English.
Deployable via Amazon SageMaker JumpStart as a chat-completions model, per AWS's SageMaker JumpStart documentation.

notes: Catalog facts (4096 max input tokens, 4096 max output tokens, /v1/chat/completions endpoint) match this chat-tuned variant's 4,096-token context window and dialogue format. Meta does not publish a chat-specific MMLU/code/reasoning table (only TruthfulQA and ToxiGen are broken out separately for Llama-2-Chat), so only TruthfulQA is listed under evaluations; ToxiGen is lower-is-better so it is not included there but is noted as an advantage instead. The huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf model card is gated (requires an accepted license to view raw text), so its content was read via a page fetch and cross-checked against Meta's public, ungated GitHub MODEL_CARD.md, which matches. No current Meta or AWS page marks this specific model deprecated or legacy, though it predates Meta's Llama 3/3.1/3.2/3.3/4 chat models already in this catalog; I found no explicit superseded/deprecation statement to cite.
